title: When does your body start using stored energy?

lines.text: When you stop eating, how many hours does it take before your body actually starts burning body fat?
lines.caps: When does your body *finally | start burning *fat?

lines.text: For the first four hours after a meal, your cells run entirely on digested glucose from your bloodstream.
lines.caps: First 4 hours run on *glucose | circulating in your *blood

lines.text: Between hours four and twelve, insulin levels drop and your liver releases stored glycogen.
Only after twelve to fourteen hours of fasting does your body exhaust easy glycogen reserves.
Your metabolism flips the biological metabolic switch, breaking down adipose tissue into fatty acids.
lines.caps: Metabolic switch flips to *burn | stored body *fat!

lines.text: By hour sixteen, ketones flood your bloodstream to fuel your brain with razor-sharp focus.
lines.caps: Ketones fuel your *brain | with clean, steady *energy

lines.text: Intermittent fasting simply allows your ancient fat-burning engine time to turn on.
lines.caps: Give your body *time | to burn its *reserves!
